summary: Since spring 2026, Ghostwriter (UAC-0057/UNC1151) has phished Ukrainian government organizations from compromised accounts using lures themed on the Prometheus online-learning platform; a ZIP with a JavaScript file (OYSTERFRESH) drops OYSTERBLUES/OYSTERSHUCK and leads to a payload assessed as Cobalt Strike. Reported by CERT-UA.
ESET: continued intelligence collection against government targets in South America.
ESET: deployed its DarkVigil toolset in Sri Lanka against Chinese-speaking individuals linked to fraud schemes.
ESET: parent of the FilthyFeline and BladedFeline subgroups; FilthyFeline resumed operations mainly against Israeli entities and some US companies.
ESET: earlier compromised a cellular data provider in Uzbekistan that FilthyFeline later targeted.
ESET: resumed operations after a quieter period, mainly against Israeli entities across sectors, with some US companies affected.
ESET: resumed targeting the drone sector with recruitment-themed social engineering.
ESET: targeted an African country, probably to monitor a North Korean worker scheme or Russian activity there.
ESET: activity declined significantly; updated PteroBox stealer and adopted PteroPSDoor and the VBScript tool Rezzuar (of Turla origin).
ESET: named as the origin of the VBScript tool Rezzuar that Gamaredon began using.
ESET: carried out a destructive attack on a Ukrainian transportation-sector manufacturer — the first documented destructive attack by a Belarus-aligned actor in Europe.
ESET: hit a Venezuelan government maritime body, likely to monitor oil shipments after the US intervention.
ESET: linked to PhiliKit, a new implant assessed as part of its SPAWN toolset for Ivanti VPN appliances.
ESET: social engineering against developers and crypto; Operation DreamJob against European drone makers; compromised the npm axios library (Operation DangerousPassword).
ESET: quick, opportunistic attacks, mainly via social engineering.
ESET: quick, opportunistic attacks, mainly via social engineering.
ESET: resurfaced in South Korea deploying TigerRAT and attempting Rook ransomware against an engineering firm linked to liquid hydrogen and nuclear equipment.
ESET: resurfaced in South Korea deploying TigerRAT and attempting Rook ransomware against an engineering firm linked to liquid hydrogen and nuclear equipment.
ESET: supply-chain compromise of a gaming platform serving China's Yanbian region to collect intelligence on refugees and defectors.
ESET: used Covenant and BeardShell implants against Ukrainian military personnel and drone organizations, and targeted logistics/transport firms outside Ukraine.
ESET: deployed several new wipers against Ukrainian government and private targets; medium-confidence attribution for a December 2025 destructive attack on a Polish energy company.
ESET: increasingly uses adversary-in-the-middle techniques for initial access and lateral movement.
ESET: increasingly uses adversary-in-the-middle techniques for initial access and lateral movement.
ESET: targeted multiple government entities across Latin America.
ESET: highly active in Southeast Asia, the US and Europe against government, engineering and maritime transport.
ESET: targeted Taiwan's healthcare sector via public-facing web servers, webshells, SoftEther VPN infrastructure and the open-source proxy BUUT.
ESET: increased spearphishing, including internal emails from compromised inboxes with high success rates.
ESET: new campaigns against the cryptocurrency sector for espionage and revenue, expanding into Uzbekistan.
ESET: experimented with ClickFix against diplomatic entities, South Korean think tanks and academia.
ESET: social engineering with an unusual focus on macOS.
ESET: exploited a WinRAR zero-day to deploy malicious DLLs and backdoors against financial, manufacturing, defense and logistics entities in the EU and Canada.
ESET: most active group targeting Ukraine; new file stealers and tunneling services; selectively deployed a Turla backdoor.
ESET: one of its backdoors was selectively deployed by Gamaredon, a rare case of cooperation between Russia-aligned groups.
ESET: deployed ZEROLOT and Sting wipers against Ukrainian government, energy, logistics and grain-sector targets.
ESET: exploited a Roundcube XSS flaw and spearphished Polish and Lithuanian companies with credential and email stealers.
Google GTIG: attributed to GRU Unit 74455; has tried to exfiltrate Telegram and Signal data, likely from devices seized in Ukraine, using WAVESIGN and INFAMOUSCHISEL (activity since at least 2023).
Google GTIG: linked by CERT-UA to Luhansk People's Republic security agencies; drone- and surveillance-themed lures deploying VERMONSTER, SPECTRUM and FIRMACHAGENT.
Google GTIG: suspected SMALLTIGER operation against South Korean defense, semiconductor and automotive manufacturers to acquire IP for North Korean R&D.
Google GTIG: infrastructure mimicking German and US defense entities with job-themed lures and credential harvesting to deploy THINWAVE and HANGMAN.V2.
Google GTIG: impersonates corporate recruiters against defense organizations; used Gemini to synthesize OSINT, profile targets and build tailored phishing personas.

Google GTIG: since at least 2022, fake job portals/offers and surveys against aerospace and defense staff; exploits third-party suppliers and remote access (Citrix, VMware); CRASHPAD and RDP session hijacking.
Google GTIG: in 2024 and May 2025, spearphished personal accounts of current and former aerospace/defense contractor employees with industry-event, job-offer and personal lures.
Google GTIG: one of the most capable China-nexus groups; edge-device access and 17 malware families against defense-industrial targets; also telecom and technology firms in the US and Asia.
Google GTIG: exploits VPN appliances and firewalls to reach MSPs, law firms and supply-chain nodes; 2025 BRICKSTORM campaign averaged 393 days of dwell time and hit aerospace and defense.
Google GTIG: China-nexus cluster exploiting edge-device zero-days to keep long-term access.
Google GTIG: linked to Volt Typhoon; 2024 reconnaissance against public login portals of North American military and defense contractors via the ARCMAZE obfuscation network and SOHO routers.
Google GTIG: historical focus on maritime-related defense technologies.
Trend Micro: rapidly weaponized a new Office zero-day within weeks and targeted war-related entities including defense ministries and border police.
Trend Micro: restructured its Kazuar toolset into a hard-to-remove botnet in which only one node per network communicates outward.
Trend Micro: posed as wartime charities and ran command-and-control from disposable paste sites.
Trend Micro: used generative AI to turn a public exploit into a large-scale scanning tool.
Trend Micro (as Earth Naga): used AI-assisted coding to build a PowerShell/C# backdoor loader.
Trend Micro: used legitimate cloud services (Microsoft Graph API, DevTunnel, SoftEther DDNS) and the Stellar blockchain for command-and-control.
Trend Micro: possible operation in which an autonomous AI agent ran scanning, exploitation, credential theft and password spraying against a Southeast Asian target.
Trend Micro: compromised the Axios maintainer account to push a remote access trojan through a package with over 100 million weekly downloads.
Trend Micro: spread malware through fake job-interview code repositories.
Trend Micro: linked to IOCONTROL, a reusable malware platform for attacking operational technology such as fuel systems.
Trend Micro (as Earth Vetala): combined its own tools with a rented backdoor from a criminal platform and resolved C2 via public blockchain queries.
CrowdStrike: used generative AI to create fake personas; activity doubled year over year.
CrowdStrike: executed AI-generated scripts during intrusions.
CrowdStrike: exploited VPN, firewall and gateway vulnerabilities for persistent footholds.

Kaspersky ICS CERT (as QuietCrabs/Subtle Werewolf): exploited CVE-2025-4427/4428 and CVE-2025-53770 to deploy KrustyLoader and Sliver against Russian targets.
Kaspersky ICS CERT (citing Positive Technologies): phishing-based espionage against Russian aerospace, logistics, manufacturing and energy organizations.
Kaspersky ICS CERT: medium-confidence attribution of DynoWiper attacks on at least 30 wind and solar farms, a manufacturer and a CHP plant in Poland; LazyWiper used at the manufacturer.

Kaspersky ICS CERT: exploited CVE-2026-21509 and CVE-2026-21513 against Ukraine, NATO allies and Eastern European maritime, transport and diplomatic targets, using PRISMEX, MiniDoor, Covenant Grunt and Filen.io C2.
Kaspersky ICS CERT: spearphishing against Middle Eastern diplomatic, maritime, financial, telecom and energy entities with RustyWater, GhostFetch, GhostBackDoor, CHAR/LampoRAT and HTTP_VIP.
Kaspersky ICS CERT: destructive hack-and-leak operations (as Handala) against Israeli and US enterprises, including Stryker, using VPN brute-forcing, NetBird, GPO-distributed wipers and VeraCrypt.
Kaspersky ICS CERT: late-2025 campaign against Russian industrial and military-industrial firms using compromised mailboxes and websites to deliver DeerStealer via HijackLoader.
Kaspersky ICS CERT: targeted Russian agro-industrial, defense and telecom firms (and Belarus) using VBShower, PowerShower and the CloudAtlas backdoor.
Kaspersky ICS CERT (as UAT-9244): attack on an Azerbaijani oil and gas company exploiting ProxyNotShell and deploying Deed RAT via DLL sideloading.
Kaspersky ICS CERT: targeted India's hydropower sector and government bodies working with Taiwan using SHARDLOADER, MINIRECON and ZOHOMURK (abusing Zoho WorkDrive).

Kaspersky ICS CERT (as Nimbus Manticore): campaigns against software and aviation staff in Saudi Arabia, Australia and elsewhere using MiniJunk, MiniFast, trojanized Zoom installers and SEO poisoning.

Kaspersky ICS CERT: scanned 12,000+ systems and brute-forced Outlook Web Access, exfiltrating data from an Egyptian aviation organization; Symantec counted at least nine organizations in nine countries.
Kaspersky ICS CERT: deployed TigerRAT and Rook ransomware against a South Korean industrial equipment engineering firm.
Kaspersky ICS CERT: deployed TigerRAT and Rook ransomware against a South Korean industrial equipment engineering firm.
Kaspersky ICS CERT: campaigns against a Vietnamese construction firm and via a FireAnt MetaKit supply-chain compromise using SPECTRALVIPER.
Kaspersky ICS CERT: targeted Ukrainian military personnel and drone makers with Covenant and BeardShell implants, plus a January 2026 CVE-2026-21509 phishing wave.
Kaspersky ICS CERT: destructive attacks in Ukraine using Group Policy-deployed wipers, RansomTuga and the Rust wiper ZeroRays (ZEROSETH) against government, energy and insurance targets.
Kaspersky ICS CERT: targeted a US engineering company supporting Ukraine via SocGholish, deploying a Mythic agent, RomCom shellcode and VIPERTUNNEL.
Kaspersky ICS CERT: Operation DreamJob against European aerospace and UAV firms using trojanized open-source software and the ScoringMathTea RAT; Comebacker variants against aerospace and defense.

Kaspersky ICS CERT: targeted Israeli and Egyptian government, utilities and transport with RMM-based access and the VAX-One and MuddyViper backdoors; reportedly accessed Jerusalem CCTV before missile strikes.
Kaspersky ICS CERT: targeted Middle Eastern aerospace, aviation and defense firms with TWOSTROKE, DEEPROOT and other backdoors; reportedly compromised maritime systems months before a missile strike.

Kaspersky ICS CERT: hijacked software updates (e.g. Sogou Pinyin) via adversary-in-the-middle with the EdgeStepper implant, targeting users in the US, Taiwan, China, Hong Kong, New Zealand and Cambodia.

Kaspersky ICS CERT (as SinisterEye): hijacked updates in China to deliver WinDealer and SpyDealer, targeting a Taiwanese defense-aviation firm, a US trade body and government entities in Greece and Ecuador.
Kaspersky ICS CERT: compromised 20+ legitimate websites and used BadAudio malware delivered via fake Chrome pop-ups and phishing.
Kaspersky ICS CERT: long-term espionage against US legal, tech and manufacturing firms targeting VMware vCenter/ESXi with BRICKSTORM, Junction and GuestConduit.
Trend Micro: Rust CRAITHNEX backdoor relaying commands through unsent Microsoft 365 draft emails, with geopolitical decoy PDFs against Southeast Asian and Indo-Pacific governments.
Trend Micro: parallel initial-access pipelines with LNK files on Google Drive, deploying SUESTAG (disguised as a Taiwanese input-method updater) and NOMASTEAL across East Asia.
Trend Micro: compromised the npm account of Axios's lead maintainer and published poisoned versions deploying a cross-platform RAT (100+ detections in 21 countries).
Trend Micro (as Void Dokkaebi): wormlike campaign of fake job-interview repositories and malicious VS Code tasks deploying DEV#POPPER RAT; 750+ repositories infected by March 2026.
Trend Micro (as Pawn Storm): exploited Office zero-day CVE-2026-21509 with the PRISMEX toolkit against Ukrainian and allied defense, border, parliamentary and weather-service targets.
Trend Micro (as Earth Dahu): exploited WinRAR CVE-2025-8088 against Ukrainian government and military via compromised official mailboxes, with C2 on Cloudflare Workers.
Trend Micro (as Void Blizzard): spoofed wartime charity sites and Signal-style lures delivering the PLUGGYAPE backdoor against Ukraine and its supporters.

Trend Micro (as Secret Blizzard): turned Kazuar into a botnet with one elected node per network and dead-drop instructions on compromised websites, targeting government and defense in Cyprus and Ukraine.
Trend Micro (as Earth Vetala): rented ChainShell backdoor, DinDoor on Deno and blockchain C2; scanned for Ivanti CVE-2026-1281 and exploited FortiOS CVE-2024-55591.
Trend Micro: linked by a US joint advisory to IOCONTROL targeting Linux-based OT and fuel-management devices; suspected Iran-linked breaches of US fuel-tank gauges in 2026.
Trend Micro: spearphished Taiwanese government agencies with ANEL and a ROAMINGMOUSE Excel macro backdoor, after earlier targeting Japanese think tanks.
Trend Micro: spearphished Taiwanese government agencies with ANEL and a ROAMINGMOUSE Excel macro backdoor, after earlier targeting Japanese think tanks.
Trend Micro (as Earth Preta): targeted government and public institutions in Southeast Asia and Europe, sideloading via trusted tools such as VLC to run PubLoad or MQsSrv in memory.
Trend Micro: focused on telecom and government, expanding from Asia-Pacific into South America, Africa and US government entities.
Trend Micro (as Earth Naga): targeted strategically valuable Taiwanese organizations and expanded to North America, the Middle East and Africa.
Trend Micro: kept persistence in Taiwanese government infrastructure and extended targeting to Taiwan's transportation sector.
Trend Micro: targeted government and telecom entities in Southeast Asia with custom malware, kernel-level rootkits and cloud-storage exfiltration.
Trend Micro: built a foothold in Latin American government infrastructure from mid-2024 using the VARGEIT backdoor.
Trend Micro: targeted Taiwan's technology sector using Microsoft Dev Tunnel and Google Calendar for covert C2.
Trend Micro (as Void Dokkaebi): fake job interviews and malicious npm packages/VS Code extensions against software and Web3 developers, deploying BeaverTail, InvisibleFerret and GolangGhost.
Trend Micro (as Earth Kumiho): targeted officials, think tanks and DPRK experts in South Korea, the US and Japan with LNK files, abusing Dropbox and GitHub, deploying KimJongRAT or HttpTroy.
Trend Micro (as Earth Imp): tax-themed lures in South Korea and invitation-themed LNKs against Russia's Foreign Ministry, using KONNI RAT.
Trend Micro (as Earth Manticore): targeted South Korean government, military and defector communities with malicious HWP documents delivering RokRAT, plus browser exploits and mobile malware.
Trend Micro: targeted cryptocurrency organizations with the macOS-focused INLETDRIFT malware.
Trend Micro: targeted cryptocurrency organizations with the macOS-focused INLETDRIFT malware.

Trend Micro (as Pawn Storm): targeted Ukraine and Western nations incl. a French government campaign (attributed April 2025), using LLM-assisted LAMEHUG, an Outlook-macro C2 backdoor and steganographic PNG payloads.
Trend Micro (as Earth Dahu): HTA spearphishing, USB-spreading modules and GammaSteel against Ukrainian defense and government; exploited WinRAR CVE-2025-8088.
Trend Micro: destructive and espionage attacks on Ukrainian energy, water, heating, logistics, rail and grain organizations using SECONDBEST, CROOKBAG, KALAMBUR and PathWiper.

Trend Micro (as Earth Koshchei): wine-tasting lures against European diplomats delivering GRAPELOADER and WINELOADER; watering-hole abuse of Microsoft device-code authentication (blocked by AWS in August 2025).
Trend Micro: attributed the destructive DynoWiper/LazyWiper attacks on about 30 Polish wind and solar farms, a private company and a heat-and-power plant (other vendors attribute this to Sandworm).
Trend Micro (as Void Blizzard): rapid, relatively simple operations; CERT-UA attributed late-2025 campaigns against Ukrainian organizations to it.
Trend Micro (as Earth Vetala): targeted telecom providers and critical infrastructure using social engineering and abused remote-management tools.
Trend Micro: exploited Ivanti Connect Secure appliances globally, deploying SPAWN implants for persistent access.
CybelAngel: active since 2020; breached at least eight US telecoms; remains active in 2026, with a House committee email breach confirmed and networks compromised in 80+ countries.

Microsoft's name for Volatile Cedar ("Lebanese Cedar"), a Lebanon-based espionage group active since at least 2012 and widely suspected of links to Hezbollah. Check Point exposed it in 2015 (Explosive RAT); ClearSky reported in 2021 that it had breached 250+ web servers in the US, UK, Israel, Lebanon, Jordan, Egypt, Saudi Arabia, the UAE and the Palestinian Authority, mainly telecoms and ISPs, using web-server exploits, the Caterpillar web shell and an updated Explosive RAT.

Operation Groundbait (ESET, May 2016): a surveillance campaign using the Prikormka malware against separatists in the self-proclaimed Donetsk and Luhansk People's Republics, plus some Ukrainian government officials and journalists. ESET assessed the operators were likely based in Ukraine.

HenBox (Palo Alto Unit 42, March 2018) is Android spyware disguised as legitimate apps (VPN and Xiaomi system apps) that targeted Uyghurs and other Chinese-speaking minorities, with a focus on Xiaomi devices. Unit 42 linked its infrastructure to the China-nexus PKPLUG espionage cluster.

Mobile surveillanceware (Lookout, May 2018): Stealth Mango (Android) and Tangelo (iOS), attributed to Pakistan's military. Delivered via a fake app store and Facebook Messenger, it stole data from government and military officials in Pakistan, India, Afghanistan, Iraq and the UAE, and captured data on US, UK, Australian and other diplomats.
ESTsecurity's name (Geumseong121) for a North Korean cluster tied to APT37/ScarCruft, which spearphished North Korean defectors, activists and South Korean targets with malicious documents.

CERT-UA identifier (September 2025) for targeted attacks on members of the Ukrainian Officers Union: malicious Excel XLL add-ins shared over Signal (e.g. a '500.zip' archive) delivered the CABINETRAT backdoor for espionage. The source does not state a Russian attribution explicitly.

Microsoft's name for DEV-0665, a Russia-linked actor tied to the HermeticWiper destructive attacks on Ukraine at the start of the 2022 invasion (related wipers IsaacWiper and CaddyWiper followed in March 2022).

Microsoft's name for i-Soon (Anxun Information Technology, also HASSIUM / DRAGNET PANDA), a Shanghai-based contractor that hacked for Chinese security services. Its internal documents leaked in February 2024, and in March 2025 the US Justice Department charged i-Soon employees and Ministry of Public Security officers over intrusions worldwide.

CrowdStrike: China-linked, state-sponsored intelligence-gathering group first seen in June 2013, targeting Tibetan and Uyghur communities through strategic web compromises, using the 9002 RAT and the Cavalry RAT.

Operators of the Shamoon (Disttrack) wiper, which destroyed some 30,000 Saudi Aramco machines in August 2012 (claimed by "Cutting Sword of Justice") and hit RasGas; Shamoon 2 struck Saudi government agencies in 2016–2017 and Shamoon 3 hit Saipem and others in December 2018. Widely attributed to Iran; later reporting links the activity to APT33/APT34-era Iranian operators.

Israel's military signals-intelligence unit. In MISP it is listed via the "Duqu Group" alias: Duqu (2011) and Duqu 2.0 (2015, which breached Kaspersky Lab and venues of the Iran nuclear talks) were widely assessed by researchers and media as Israeli operations, though no vendor formally attributed them to the unit.

Caution: likely not state-sponsored. Microsoft described Storm-1167 (June 2023) as running a multi-stage adversary-in-the-middle phishing and business-email-compromise campaign against banking and financial organizations, using an AiTM kit it developed. It is on this list only because MISP tags it with a country (Indonesia).
Caution: likely a hacktivist group, not a state actor. CrowdStrike's "Jackal" names denote hacktivists; MISP lists the alias TunisianCyberArmy. Neither source gives a detailed public profile.
Caution: likely a hacktivist group, not a state actor. CrowdStrike's "Jackal" names denote hacktivists; MISP lists the alias Vikingdom. Neither source gives a detailed public profile.
Duplicate row: this MISP entry is the same group as APT35 (Charming Kitten / Mint Sandstorm). See APT35 for its full description, TTPs and recent activity.

Proofpoint's name for the Iranian group otherwise tracked as Charming Kitten / APT35 / Mint Sandstorm; see APT35. Proofpoint describes TA453 using compromised accounts, malware and confrontational lures against academics, policy experts and journalists.
Proofpoint's name for a North Korean cluster within the Kimsuky family (malware distribution, phishing, intelligence collection and cryptocurrency theft); see Kimsuky.
Duplicate row: misspelled MISP entry for the CrowdStrike name POISONOUS PANDA (see Poisonous Panda). No public profile found.

Microsoft: since January 2026 shifted to large-scale phishing from compromised websites against Ukrainian individuals and institutions plus NGOs, think tanks, governments and financial institutions supporting Ukraine (100+ organizations, mainly US/UK), using the new "RedFlick" scheduled-task delivery to install the CosmicPulse backdoor.

Microsoft: since January 2026 shifted to large-scale phishing from compromised websites against Ukrainian individuals and institutions plus NGOs, think tanks, governments and financial institutions supporting Ukraine (100+ organizations, mainly US/UK), using the new "RedFlick" scheduled-task delivery to install the CosmicPulse backdoor.

Trellix: ported BellaCiao to C++ (BellaCPP), hardened PowerLess, ran a January–June 2025 phishing kit against Israeli academics, technologists and journalists, added video-conference lures; a December 2025 leak linked it to Moses Staff.
Trellix: SpearSpecter campaign using WhatsApp outreach to senior government and defense officials, delivering the TameCat PowerShell backdoor.
Recorded Future: Google reported in February 2026 that it used Gemini to develop malicious tools and build trust-based phishing personas.
Trellix: targeted Iraqi government entities with Veaty and Spearal backdoors and exploited CVE-2024-30088 against UAE and Gulf government organizations.
Trellix: distributed the WezRat stealer through spearphishing impersonating security bodies.
Trellix: continued aerospace, defense, telecom and aviation espionage using GhostLine, LightRail and DeepRoot against targets in Denmark, Sweden, Portugal, Israel and the UAE.
Trellix: resurfaced with Foudre, Tonnerre and MaxPinner, paused 8–27 January 2026 during an Iranian internet blackout, and expanded targeting to 20+ countries.
Trellix: compromised Oman's Foreign Ministry email and sent macro documents to 100+ diplomatic recipients in 30 countries about Hamas ceasefire negotiations.
Proofpoint: credential phishing against a Middle Eastern government entity sent from a compromised Iraqi foreign ministry account, using a fake Outlook Web App page and conflict lures.

Proofpoint (Winter Vivern): emails impersonating a European Council President spokesperson targeted European and Middle Eastern government organizations — its first observed Middle East government targeting.
Proofpoint: long-running espionage thread impersonating a think-tank researcher, pivoting on 8 March 2026 to OneDrive-themed credential phishing against a US think tank.
Recorded Future: Operation Olalampo from 26 January 2026 delivered four new malware families to MENA targets via spearphishing.
Recorded Future (as Nimbus Manticore): lures impersonating aviation and software firms against US, European and Middle Eastern targets; AI-assisted development of the MiniFast backdoor.
Recorded Future: researchers recreated its PLC reconnaissance workflow with an AI agent; group remains focused on exposed ICS.

LAC (via Cyber Security News, Feb 2025): "RevivalStone" campaign against Japanese manufacturing, materials and energy organizations — SQL injection in an ERP system to deploy web shells and a new Winnti malware version with a RAT and rootkit.

Check Point: exploited WebDAV zero-day CVE-2025-33053 via malicious .url files against government and defense entities in Turkey, Qatar, Egypt and Yemen, delivering the Mythic-based Horus Agent; patched June 2025.

Lumen Black Lotus Labs (via Help Net Security): used a shifting relay network ("Silent Train"), built before the December 2023 KV-botnet takedown, to hide its most sensitive intrusions; exploited zero-days in enterprise management, SD-WAN and other control-plane systems against US government, telecom, defense contractors, MSPs and critical infrastructure (Hawaii, California, Texas most targeted).

Microsoft: shifted to compromising IT supply chains (remote management tools, cloud apps, MSPs) using stolen API keys, edge-device zero-days (Ivanti, Palo Alto, Citrix, Exchange), password spraying and OAuth app abuse to exfiltrate mail and SharePoint data via Graph API.

CYFIRMA (via The Hacker News): spearphishing with ZIPs containing LNKs disguised as PDFs against Indian government, academic and strategic entities, deploying a new RAT with antivirus-aware persistence.

Acronis TRU (via The Hacker News, moderate confidence): ongoing campaign against Afghan telecoms and South Asian critical infrastructure (incl. Indian government and energy) using fake VPN installers and telecom tools to deliver the new PATCHCORD backdoor.

Kaspersky (via The Hacker News, March 2025): targeted maritime and logistics firms across South/Southeast Asia, the Middle East and Africa plus nuclear power, telecom, IT and diplomatic entities, using CVE-2017-11882 documents, the ModuleInstaller downloader and the StealerBot toolkit.
Microsoft (via Security Affairs, March 2025): used Qilin ransomware in limited attacks — its first use of a third-party ransomware after previously deploying only custom ransomware.

EclecticIQ (as Bitter/TA397): spearphished Pakistan Telecommunication Company staff in 5G, DevOps and satellite roles during the May 2025 India–Pakistan escalation, delivering a WmRAT variant via an IQY/Excel macro.
Sygnia: exploited a Cisco NX-OS zero-day to deploy malware on Nexus switches, after earlier abusing legacy F5 BIG-IP appliances for about three years of persistence in an East Asian firm.
NSFOCUS: ranked among the most active groups in June 2026; South Asian campaigns hit government agencies in Pakistan, India and Cambodia and military institutions in Sri Lanka.
NSFOCUS: spearphishing PDF impersonating a Ukrainian National Guard notice against Ukrainian government and military personnel; USB propagation module.
NSFOCUS: listed as notably active in June 2026.
NSFOCUS: ranked among the most active APT groups in April and June 2026.
NSFOCUS: "Operation Xenofiscal" against Afghanistan's Ministry of Finance and provincial fiscal offices — its first known targeting outside India.

NSFOCUS: "Operation TrustTrap" pre-registered 16,800+ spoofed domains impersonating government portals to steal credentials and card data (US state agencies, Indian government, UK NHS-style services).
NSFOCUS: "Operation Neusploit" against Ukrainian and allied defense institutions using zero-days CVE-2026-21509 and CVE-2026-21513 in an MSHTML-based .lnk attack.
NSFOCUS: among the three most active groups in April 2026.

Sekoia TDR: watering-hole campaign (assessed "moderate to high confidence" as APT29) via compromised sites and a one-week hijack of the Plerdy analytics script (Aug 27–Sep 3), mostly hitting Ukrainian sites incl. military and defense makers; fingerprinting served n-day exploit chains for iOS 16.7/18.5 (DarkSword kit; CVE-2025-43529, CVE-2024-27834, CVE-2026-20700, CVE-2025-14174, CVE-2025-43510, CVE-2025-43520) and Android Chrome (CVE-2026-3910, CVE-2025-27038) to steal cookies, credentials, messages and Keychain data without persistence.

Symantec Threat Hunter Team: intrusions at a law enforcement agency, a naval shipbuilder and a military aircraft engine manufacturer in two NATO states; macro Word lures delivering the Hookedge backdoor (webhook.site tasking), new reflective loader ld.exe, SSH tunnelling and NTLM capture; launcher last seen 2026-09-24.

FortiGuard Labs: espionage campaign against South Asian organizations ("high confidence" BITTER) using LNK/ftp.exe, VHDX+MSI and WebDAV chains to deploy new PapRAT backdoor (C++ and Rust variants) plus WmRAT, with diplomatic/military-themed decoys.

ESET: China-aligned group hijacked Sogou Input Method's update/brand-promotion mechanism via DNS hijacking (campaign from 2026-07-01) to deliver the modular .NET DarkVigil (FDMTP) backdoor to victims in Hong Kong, Thailand, Japan, Vietnam, Oman and Sri Lanka; tracked as distinct from Mustang Panda.

Joint advisory AA26-281A (FBI, CISA, NSA, NCSC-UK, ASD's ACSC, Canada, Japan, NZ, Spain): exposed Integrity Technology Group as enabler of Flax Typhoon/Ethereal Panda activity against US critical infrastructure, law enforcement, education and religious organizations and victims in Southeast Asia and Africa; tools incl. MicroScan, EBurst, SoftEther VPN, office-cli M365 exfiltration; exploited CVE-2019-11510, CVE-2021-22205, CVE-2023-22894 and older bugs.
Google GTIG (now tracking it as CALANQUE ION): continues to use LLMs including Gemini to augment reconnaissance and targeted social engineering.

Genians (via Korean press; "medium" confidence Kimsuky): spear-phishing impersonating a National Assembly member's secretary against seminar attendees; a "honorarium" lure delivered via webmail large-attachment link an archive with an LNK disguised as a Hangul document; infrastructure overlapped past Kimsuky operations.

ESET (attributes Cereal to Turla "with high confidence"): compromised Microsoft Exchange servers of national government organizations in Kazakhstan (seen 28 Nov 2025) and Romania (23 Dec 2025) with the new Cereal toolset (CerealLoader, CerealRunner, CerealNeuron passive backdoor, CerealBox Exchange transport agent collecting email to/from NATO and EU addresses, CerealHermit, CerealIron, CerealMoth); the Exchange servers themselves served as C&C; initial access vector not determined.

FBI and USSS: attributed the ~$6.3 billion theft from Binance to North Korea's TraderTraitor and urged exchanges to block derived addresses; Binance post-mortem describes a months-long campaign from June 2026 using fake job interviews, a malicious coding-test repository and "AI coding tool" installer, EDR-evading endpoint compromise, lateral movement from 20 Oct and abuse of wallet-signing credentials. North Korea denied involvement.

FBI (FaceStealer scheme, attributed to North Korean cyber actors; THN links it to BlueNoroff/UNC1069 and Kaspersky's GhostCall): over $400 million stolen in 18 months from crypto/Web3 founders, executives and open-source developers via hijacked Telegram/LinkedIn/Slack accounts, Calendly invites, typosquatted Zoom/Teams sites, pre-recorded or deepfake video of trusted contacts and fake "audio fix"/SDK-update lures; DoJ seized the cloud infrastructure and 900+ victim webcam recordings.

Google Threat Intelligence Group (Russia-linked COLD RELIC, formerly tracked as COLDRIVER/UNC4057; the US government associates it with Russia's FSB): used data and identities stolen in a late-2025 compromise of one US organization's Google Workspace to impersonate an employee and breach a second US organization in 2026; MFA push fatigue via residential proxies, Entra ID credential phishing, Super Admin abuse, rogue MFA devices and passkeys for persistence, Google Takeout exfiltration; targets historically government officials, defense contractors and NGOs in Europe and North America; no malware or CVEs named.

CloudSEK (exposed operator server; Silent Lynx "with high confidence" on tooling, Kazakhstan nexus "medium confidence"; Central Asia-focused espionage): intrusion at Tajikistan's national railway (mid-Aug to at least 10 Oct 2026) and the Tajik government EDO document platform holding Ministry of Defence correspondence, an Uzbekistan forestry GeoServer, Turkmenistan lures built in Oct 2026 for an upcoming campaign, and a Kyrgyzstan payload set; Laplas and Chvost TLS reverse shells, PowerShell reverse shell, LNK phishing, fscan, Ligolo, GOST, Inveigh, Responder, NetExec, Impacket, Metasploit and the Hermes open-source AI agent running DeepSeek models.

Google Threat Intelligence Group / Mandiant (suspected PRC-nexus espionage actor ARMORY CASTLE, formerly UNC5221): after a BeyondTrust Remote Support zero-day foothold (CVE-2026-102764), exploited vCenter zero-day CVE-2026-123890 (VMware Directory Service SRP session-key disclosure, patched 19 Nov 2026) in early September 2026 with the Go tool BONESAW, then SAWSNAKE (vCenter SAML bypass / Golden SAML), BEARBONES (Dropbear-based backdoor), LAZYBONES (Slack C2) and SLIMSAVAGE/CAGEMATCH JSP web shells on internal Linux appliances; CrowdStrike reported abuse of ESX logging flaw CVE-2026-41709 to reduce audit visibility.

ESET Research (Russia-aligned Gorbag; ESET assesses it "may be cooperating with other groups as an initial access broker"): espionage against Ukraine only — law enforcement and justice bodies, front-line city councils, defense entities and a transport hub for foreign military aid; macro .xlsm lures in 2025, then weaponized RAR archives exploiting WinRAR CVE-2025-8088 in early 2026; Prime ReverseShell (PS2EXE PowerShell reverse shell) and the self-deleting BeautyStealer browser/file stealer (Telegram or FastAPI C2).

Check Point Research (CopperDragon assessed as a possible "digital quartermaster" developing the Sparrow framework for China-nexus actors incl. FamousSparrow, Earth Estries, Tropic Trooper and UAT-9244): three clusters — SilentDelivery (watering holes on government, shipping and IT/research sites; fake "Certificate Fix" MSI delivering SquadC and SparrowDoor; visitors in Czech Republic, Germany, France, Taiwan, Nepal, Hong Kong, Indonesia), OceanGate (Asian government and critical infrastructure; AnnobinDoor, SparrowShell, Copper* tools) and DarkWire (Latin American telecoms and foreign-affairs/justice bodies; CopperLoader, CopperDoor/SparroWocky, CopperDNS MX tunnelling), the latter tied via infrastructure to a FamousSparrow domain.

CYFIRMA (suspected DPRK campaign; identified as Lazarus, via Korea JoongAng Daily): staging exploitation of two "PHP2Shell" remote code execution flaws in PHP core on Windows against ~216 vulnerable servers in 10 countries (30 in South Korea; also Japan, US, Thailand, Indonesia, India) across government, finance, ICT, critical infrastructure, logistics/aviation, manufacturing and e-commerce; web shells and scanning nodes, expanding to 581 hosts after obtaining admin credentials.

Kaspersky GReAT (Operation FlashHole, "a cyberespionage campaign attributed to the Lazarus APT group"): spear-phishing and abuse of the CrossWeb EX security software (possible vulnerability per an AhnLab advisory, no CVE) against at least three South Korean organizations in construction, software and wire-communication equipment manufacturing; new TouchHub and ClientHub tools, an updated LPEClient using ML-KEM-1024 post-quantum encryption (PQC use traced to at least September 2024) and a Dropbox-based variant; AI use noted.

Palo Alto Unit 42 (TGR-STA-0049, also tracked as REF7707, Earth Alux, Ink Dragon): campaign since at least July 2025 against Southeast Asian government entities, initial access via unpatched Microsoft Exchange servers and phishing with decoy PDFs (one impersonating a Myanmar election notice); new HTTP/3 (QUIC)-capable RATs PerfectPioneer (Go) and modular KUKURAT (C++, observed since March 2026) alongside Squidoor/FINALDRAFT, ASPXSpy, Godzilla and Suo5 web shells.

Dream Research Labs (attributed to Mustang Panda "with high confidence"; "a China-aligned attacker"): lure targeting Philippine government officials ahead of the 49th ASEAN Summit in Manila - a decoy PDF impersonating a Laos Ministry of Foreign Affairs bilateral meeting agenda naming five officials (archive assembled 29 Oct, reply deadline 30 Oct; metadata names Brunei, suggesting reuse across ASEAN); signed Wondershare BugSplatHD.exe sideloads BugSplat.dll, which runs shellcode from BugSplatRC.dat to load PlugX; C2 uncvlizd[.]com (re-registered 15 Sep 2026, live 27 Oct to 4 Nov); Dream says the scope and any successful infections remain unconfirmed.

Dream Research Labs (via The Hacker News; "Iran-nexus", "Iran state-aligned threat actor"; overlaps Elastic REF8685, Palo Alto CL-STA-1178, UNC5795 and Dust Specter; Dream assesses with medium confidence that UNC5795 and UNC5187 "may represent related sub-clusters within the broader APT34 group"): compromise of a high-profile Israeli individual and a Kurdistan Region of Iraq government cloud environment; SHELBYLOADER (HOTAIR, ShelbyLoader V2), SHELBYC2 (AEROSTAT, GitHub-based C2), Blackwood tunnel, StarkMeet decoy app, .csproj AppDomainManager injection and DLL sideloading, credential-phishing domains; active since at least September 2024.
